narrative.overview:
This is a design system built for someone who has been burned before. They've seen the SaaS cream generators, the purple blob heroes, the identical feature grids. They know exactly what they need and have no patience for packaging that costs them trust. The Tanship design system earns its place the same way good tooling earns it: by not getting in the way, by working exactly as expected, and by looking like it was made by someone who uses what they build.

The system is structural, not decorative. Density and contrast create interest. Ironwood, the core dark near-black tone, carries the weight of nearly every surface decision: it is the foreground in light mode, the background in dark mode, the card surface that lifts from the dark ground. Circuit Teal appears only where it means something: in the logo, as a punctuation mark, never as ambient decoration. Motion is minimal: an active button press is the most animation most elements will ever perform.

Dark mode is not a feature. It is the face of this brand. A solo founder at 11pm, terminal glow on their face, reading a landing page to decide if this stack saves them a weekend. That scene is the design brief. Light mode serves reading and daytime use; dark mode serves the identity.
keyCharacteristics: Flat-by-default with ring-based depth, never shadow-first
Square corners on marketing surfaces; gently rounded on UI components
Two typefaces, one voice: Figtree (structure) and Nunito Sans (reading)
Ironwood and its tonal steps do the work; Circuit Teal is reserved
Active feedback on every interactive element: translate-y-px on press
Every element earns its space; no decoration that adds no signal

rules.name: The Ironwood Economy
rules.body: Ironwood is the only color that changes structural meaning between modes. Every surface, every elevated layer, every primary action traces back to this one color's tonal scale. Secondary and Tertiary colors are visitors, not residents.

rules.name: The Circuit Reserve
rules.body: Circuit Teal appears on the logo and in maximum three additional elements per screen. It is never used as a background fill on large surfaces. Its rarity is the accent; spend it only where the eye needs to land.

rules.name: The One-Font-Per-Role Rule
rules.body: Figtree is for structural labels and headings. Nunito Sans is for reading. Never swap them. Don't introduce a third family for code or mono unless a monospace element is explicitly required by a feature.

rules.name: The Scale Ratio Rule
rules.body: Minimum 1.25 ratio between any two adjacent type steps. Flat type scales are prohibited: if two elements look the same size, one of them shouldn't exist.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are on the plane at rest. The only element that lifts is a dialog. Hover states shift color, not elevation. Sidebar panels use a border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Ring-First Rule
rules.body: When a container needs visual separation, reach for ring-1 ring-foreground/10 before any shadow value. If a ring is insufficient, reconsider whether the element needs separation at all.

dos: Do use ring-1 ring-foreground/10 as the primary container boundary
Do use rounded-none for all CTA buttons on marketing surfaces
Do use Ironwood as the primary button fill in light mode and card surface in dark mode
Do keep Circuit Teal for the logo and at most two additional accent moments per page
Do apply active:translate-y-px to every interactive button
Do write display copy at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 3.75rem) with tracking-tight
Do cap body line length at 65-75ch
Do use focus-visible:ring-2 for all interactive elements
Do write dark mode as the primary brand identity surface
donts: Don't use generic SaaS cream: soft gradients, rounded cards, purple-to-blue hero blobs, pastel feature grids
Don't copy ShipFast or similar boilerplate-marketing aesthetics
Don't use decorative shadows on cards, nav elements, or page sections
Don't add decoration that adds no signal: background patterns, floating blobs, colored dividers
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe
Don't use the hero-metric template: big number, small label, gradient accent
Don't round CTA buttons on marketing surfaces
